commits.messageBody:
Triaged 20 CodeRabbit inline comments against the rebased 32-file diff.
6 were on files not in this PR (chunker, search_hybrid) and are dropped
by the rebase. The 14 in-scope items are resolved as follows:

Critical
- dataset_cobalt/IInstance.py: wrap `q.metadata = dict(...)` assignment
  in try/except so the shared `Question` Pydantic schema (which does not
  declare `metadata` and does not set `extra='allow'`) no longer crashes
  the pipeline at runtime. Skips gracefully with a debug log.

Major
- dataset_cobalt/IInstance.py: clear `q.questions = []` before
  `addQuestion(text)` so template prompts don't leak into emitted items.
- dataset_cobalt/services.json: remove `file` from the test profile's
  `profiles` array; the `file` profile has no default `file_path` and
  would fail the `count >0` service-test assertion.
- test/nodes/test_dataset_cobalt.py: extend session cleanup to also
  evict `nodes.dataset_cobalt.*` from sys.modules and document why the
  fixture must stay session-scoped (lazy `from cobalt import Dataset`
  imports inside dataset_loader would break with earlier restoration).

Minor
- eval_cobalt/__init__.py: sort `__all__` (RUF022).
- dataset_cobalt/IGlobal.py, eval_cobalt/IGlobal.py: add targeted
  `# noqa: BLE001` on intentional broad validation-to-warning catches.
- dataset_cobalt/dataset_loader.py: add `from None` to path-traversal
  raise inside except (B904).
- eval_cobalt/evaluators/format_check.py: loosen JSON fence regex to
  accept single-line and trailing-whitespace variants.
- eval_cobalt/evaluators/grounding.py: return `None` for stop-word-only
  sentences and skip them in the mean so trivial sentences no longer
  inflate grounding scores.
- docs/README-cobalt-testing.md: document `context` as `str | list[str]`
  to match the evaluator contract used by the RAG tests.
- test/cobalt/cobalt.toml: clarify `p95` is an upper-bound threshold on
  a 0.0-1.0 higher-is-better scale (not a worst-case metric).
- test/cobalt/conftest.py: use `sys.path.append` with a duplicate guard
  instead of `insert(0, ...)` so the test dir can't shadow packages.
- test/nodes/test_dataset_cobalt.py: use `repr(context)` in the gold-
  answer leak assertion to catch nested/stringified forms.

All 125 existing cobalt unit tests pass after these changes.

commits.messageBody:
The prompt node emits a Question it assembles itself rather than
forwarding the one it received, and copied only the question text. Every
evaluation pipeline shaped like examples/cobalt-evaluation.pipe therefore
scored 0.0 on every item: dataset_cobalt attached the reference to
metadata['expected'], prompt dropped it, and eval_cobalt found no
reference to score against.

Forward metadata through the rebuild using the shared
ai.common.utils.merge_metadata helper, so the keys of every collected
question are unioned onto the emitted one. metadata is never rendered
into the prompt, so the reference still never reaches the model.

Also reset the accumulator in open(). The engine constructs one
IInstance per filter instance and calls open() once per object, so
without a reset a second object inherited the first object's collected
text, a duplicate copy of the configured instructions, and its metadata.
The text and instruction leaks predate this change; forwarding metadata
would have turned them from an obviously-empty result into a wrong
reference and a plausible-looking score. Every other accumulating node
(tool_guild, tool_n8n, guardrails, answer_documents) resets the same way.

Add nodes/test/cobalt/test_pipeline_metadata_hop.py, which wires the real
dataset_cobalt, prompt, ai.common.llm_base and eval_cobalt classes
together over the real rocketride Question/Answer models, stubbing only
the engine boundary and the provider call. Every other Cobalt test drives
one node behind mocks, which is why this survived four review rounds.

Correct the Question.metadata caveat in the Python SDK docs, which named
prompt as a node that drops metadata.

Refs #1644

commits.messageBody:
Four correctness gaps found while working through the open review
threads:

- A non-finite score reported a PASS. max(0.0, min(1.0, float('nan')))
  is 1.0 in CPython, so a NaN or inf score — reachable from a custom
  evaluator or an upstream cobalt result — was clamped into a perfect
  result. Non-finite and non-numeric scores now coerce to 0.0, and a NaN
  threshold can never be satisfied.

- Per-call threshold overrides bypassed the clamp applied in __init__.
  _resolve_threshold now clamps finite overrides to [0.0, 1.0] and falls
  back to the configured threshold for NaN or non-numeric input.

- The exported framework evaluate_* functions never clamped threshold at
  all, so a caller passing -1 passed everything and 2 failed everything.
  They now share a clamp_threshold helper.

- grounding compared an unrounded average against the threshold while
  returning a rounded score, letting a result report a score below
  threshold with passed=True at the boundary. It now rounds before
  comparing, matching relevance.

Remove 'not', 'nor' and 'neither' from STOP_WORDS. Both relevance and
grounding score by content-word overlap, so discarding negations made a
flat contradiction score identically to the correct answer (both 1.0).
To be precise about what this buys: the negated sentence now scores lower
(relevance 0.825, grounding 0.75 against a matching reference) but still
passes at any sane threshold. This removes the blindness, it does not
solve negation — that needs polarity-aware comparison rather than
bag-of-words overlap. The new tests assert score direction only, never a
verdict flip. Measured across all 73 evaluator calls in the suite, no
existing score or verdict moved.

Refs #1644
commits.messageHeadline: fix(nodes): harden the Cobalt evaluators against unusable scores

commits.messageBody:
load_from_items validated only that its input was a list, so a scalar
element survived the loader and raised AttributeError: 'str' object has
no attribute 'get' deep inside to_questions. The node boundaries turn
that into a bare warning and an empty dataset, so a user pasting
["a", "b"] into the inline items field got a silent no-op run with a
meaningless message.

The file paths already guarded this with a nested helper. Promote it to a
module-level _require_item_mappings and call it from both, so the error
names the offending index, the actual type, and the source. The textarea
path is validated after parsing, not only the list path.

Narrow the ImportError guard in eval_cobalt/__init__.py. It exists so the
pure-python evaluators subpackage can be imported without the engine, but
catching every ImportError meant a real defect — a typo in a submodule
import, or a genuinely missing dependency — silently exported
IGlobal = None and surfaced much later as an AttributeError on NoneType.
Verified that the intended case raises with exc.name == 'rocketlib'.

Replace the `if CONFIG: pass / else:` inversion in eval_cobalt/IGlobal
with the early return dataset_cobalt/IGlobal already uses.

Drop four `# noqa: BLE001` directives, keeping their rationale as plain
comments. This repo selects only E, F, Q and D, so BLE001 is not enabled
and suppressing it marked a rule that can never fire — the point
@asclearuc conceded on the last round, applied to the suppressions this
PR had added. The pre-existing ARG001 suppression in nodes/test/conftest.py
is left alone as out of scope, and the E402/F401 directives stay because
those rules are live.

Refs #1644

before other and bump other's position. Pre-declaring a category is

entry. Swept the other consumers (sidebars.ts, spine.js, redirects.ts) —

and a new Evaluation section for eval_cobalt placed to match its category
position. Confirmed the file is hand-maintained — nothing generates it,
and every reference to it is inbound — so the rows will not be clobbered.

commits.messageBody:
The guide documented evaluate_grounding's context parameter as
`str | list[str]`, describing a concatenation the code does not do:
grounding.py:90 takes `context: str`, and passing a list raises
AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'lower'. Every caller
already joins its documents. Narrow the doc to match the code rather than
widening the code to match the doc.

cobalt.toml presented itself, and was presented by the guide, as *the*
quality-gate configuration. Nothing in this repository reads it — the
offline pytest gates under nodes/test/cobalt/experiments/ hard-code their
own thresholds. Say so in both places so editing it is not mistaken for
changing what pytest enforces, and correct the p95 comment, which
described the 95th percentile as a worst case when it is the upper tail.

Also: give the remaining bare fence a language (MD040), document the
threshold range on all three evaluators, correct the directory listing to
name the test modules and identify nodes/test/cobalt/evaluators/ as
re-export shims, point custom-evaluator authors at the canonical location
under nodes/src/nodes/eval_cobalt/evaluators/, and fix the last two stale
test/nodes/ paths.

Guard the RAG experiment's per-sentence check against grounding's
score=None entries, which it compared with `<` directly. Current fixtures
never produce one, so this was a latent TypeError waiting on the next
fixture edit; skipped sentences are now excluded from both the numerator
and the denominator instead of counting as grounded.

Refs #1644

Three corrections the sync surfaced, none of which changes what the nodes do:

- `eval_cobalt/services.json` carried a `"tests"` key that the harness does
  not read. The harness key is `test`, and a real `test` block is not
  workable here: the dynamic runner always wires the node under test
  downstream of a webhook (nodes/test/framework/pipeline.py), and
  `eval_cobalt`'s only input lane is `answers`, which a webhook cannot
  produce without a live LLM. Writing an unvalidatable block would run in
  the required Build job on three OSes. Dropped the key and left a JSONC
  comment recording why, pointing at
  `nodes/test/cobalt/test_eval_cobalt.py`, which covers all three cases the
  key described verbatim.

- `test_pipeline_metadata_hop.py` loads `llm_base.py` from source against a
  dependency-free stub package. Develop's a25ea7a8 (#1780) added
  `from ai.common.llm_adapter import turn_usage` to that module, so the
  suite now hits `ModuleNotFoundError` on import. Stub the adapter with a
  no-op `turn_usage` scope rather than loading the real one, which pulls
  `ai.common.utils.flatten_content_blocks` that the stub does not carry.
  The suite asserts on metadata, so a `None` usage read is harmless — it
  just leaves `answer.tokens` unset.

- `format_check.py`: collapse the two `str.startswith` calls into the
  tuple form.

apply_transforms wrapped both `from cobalt import Dataset` and the
_apply_transforms_cobalt call it guards in the same try. An ImportError
raised from inside cobalt -- a lazy third-party import in Dataset.from_items,
.filter, .sample or .slice -- was therefore caught as "cobalt not installed"
and silently rerouted through the pure-Python fallback, so a half-broken
install returned differently-transformed items with only a debug line.

already how load_from_file:149-159 guards the same dependency. Behaviour with
cobalt absent, and with cobalt working, is unchanged.

commits.messageBody:
basalt-ai-cobalt was spelled out with the same specifier in three files.
Two of them have to stay: depends() resolves requirements.txt relative to
the importing node's own directory and no-ops when it is absent
(rocketlib depends.py:1224), so a node that does not declare its driver
does not get one, and the repo has no include-based alternative in use --
none of the ~122 node requirements files uses -r or -c.

The third was the one that could actually drift. nodes/test/cobalt is
outside every mechanism that reconciles the other two: lock-node-deps.yml
compiles only nodes/src/nodes/**/requirements.txt into constraints.lock,
and dependabot's pip ecosystem covers /nodes/src/nodes but not /nodes/test.
A bump to the nodes would have left the test harness pinned to the old
range with nothing to catch it.

Point it at eval_cobalt's file with -r instead, so the harness installs
whatever the node it exercises asks for. Verified with
`uv pip compile nodes/test/cobalt/requirements.txt`: resolves through the
include to basalt-ai-cobalt==0.2.3.

Comment the two node files with why they are separate and what gates them,
following the cross-file note in anonymize/requirements.txt.

commits.messageBody:
The cross-node tests wired the same chain as the example but from items
written out in the test file, which leaves the example free to drift into a
shape the tests never see -- the gap that let a reference-plumbing break
survive four review rounds.

Read the example instead and drive the graph it declares. The dataset hop now
runs through the node's own config resolver
(IEndpoint._sourceConfigFromTask digs the component out of taskConfig the way
the engine hands it over), the real DatasetLoader, scanObjects, and
renderObject -- four hops that only exist in source mode, which is the mode
the example configures and which no other test in this file reached.

Adds 8 tests in two classes:

* structural -- every input.from resolves to a declared component, the
  pipeline's source is the dataset node and is in Source mode, every provider
  is one this node tree registers (matched on the protocol in
  services*.json, since `response_answers` is registered by the `response`
  node rather than by a directory of its own), and the evaluator reads the
  answers lane the LLM writes.
* behavioural -- the reference is asserted at each hop by name, then every
  item in the example's own inline dataset is scored against the example's
  own threshold. A wrong answer must still fail, and no reference may appear
  in a prompt the example sends.

Values come from the file, not from copies of it: questions, references and
the 0.6 threshold are all read out of the pipe, so editing the example moves
the assertions with it.

Offline run over the shipped example: 3 items, cobalt_score [1.0, 1.0, 1.0],
cobalt_passed [true, true, true] -- previously 0.0 on every item.
pytest nodes/test/cobalt: 223 passed, 2 skipped, in both collection orders.
